ledger.claim: The trace governs the threshold test and it establishes a deviation on this trip: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km, which is 36.3% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate pass — 36.3% clears the 20% test and 2.98 km clears the 0.8 km test — so the excess is established on the trace figure the clause makes governing, not on the rounded trip_record copy.

The three artifacts describe the same trip — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-00103 with the same 08:07:20 pickup/start window — and the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 175 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and 100% coverage. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire, so the excess stands at the measured figure and no independent corroboration of it is required.

The rider accepts that the LTA closure of Braddell Road (valid 05:30 to 12:00, overlapping the trip window, with 33 trace fixes inside the advisory geometry) exonerates the driver's distance to the POL-RD-03 cap: the justified excess is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km), which is 2.98 km, so the whole of the excess is excused and no distance or time refund is sought. What POL-RD-03 does not do is move the ERP gantries onto the rider, who did not cause the closure and did not choose the CTE.

The rider is being made to pay $4.00 of expressway ERP that her route would never have generated: trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and both charged gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 — carry on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(2), where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03 the distance and time charges stand, but off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip; the $4.00 claimed is well inside that cap.

The CTE detour was not rider-caused, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar that ERP refund: the only chat message announcing the diversion is the driver's — 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' — and the rider's 'ok' is an acknowledgement, not an instruction identifying a place or road, and neither message carries a waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04's exoneration cannot be run on this record, and no distance may be excluded on the strength of that exchange.

On the closure branch the fare artifact itself publishes the arithmetic: with the closure-adjusted optimal of 11.18 km and 28.6 minutes, the recomputed fare is $20.993 against a charged total of $25.12, a refund of $4.127, rounded up to the nearest $0.05 as $4.15. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding the $4.00 of ERP on top of that — the ERP is already comprehended in the recomputation because the recomputed fare carries only on-optimal-route gantries, and here that figure is zero — so $4.15 is the single amount the rider should receive, and it comfortably meets her request for at least the ERP.

Nothing on this record requires escalation, so the tribunal can rule on the money: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no timestamps run backwards, the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, the traffic advisory is present and COMPLETE rather than missing — so neither POL-RD-13 nor POL-RD-10(5) is engaged — and the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling.

No impairment discount applies to the rider's case: every artifact she relies on — trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown and traffic advisory — is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02(2) does not drag the ruling below the 0.70 floor and no disclosure of impairment is owed.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration gate for claimants with four or more claims in 60 days is not triggered and no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded of her. The profile is cited only for that test, as POL-GEN-01 requires, and nothing else on it bears on this trip.

The whole of the measured excess is exonerated by the closure under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, a road the optimal route itself traverses; it is valid 05:30 to 12:00 on the trip date, so it overlaps the 08:07-08:36 trip window; and the trace enters the advisory geometry with 33 fixes inside it (EV-GPS-00103). The exoneration cap is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, which is exactly the measured excess. The driver's diversion falls entirely inside the cap and attracts no distance penalty.

The rider chose the CTE, so no ERP refund is due. EV-CHAT-00103 records the driver naming the Braddell closure and the CTE routing at 08:12:30 and the rider answering "ok" at 08:12:58, sixty-eight seconds before the first CTE gantry was charged at 08:14:06. That assent is a rider instruction within POL-RD-04, and the trace corroborates it: the vehicle runs past both CTE gantries at 0.0 m and 40.25 m (EV-GPS-00103). On a detour the rider authorised, POL-RD-09(3) provides that no ERP refund is due. The rider's assertion that he "did not choose to go on the CTE" is contradicted by his own message.

If the closure alone is treated as the cause, the refund must still be run against the closure-adjusted optimal and not the booked one. POL-RD-02, applied to the adjusted optimal of 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km (duration 28.6 min), gives a recomputed fare of SGD 20.993 against a charged total of SGD 25.12 - a refund of SGD 4.13, rounded up to SGD 4.15. That is the ceiling; it is not the SGD 8.49 an unadjusted comparison would produce, and it is far short of the SGD 9.00 the rider contests. The rider himself accepts the diversion was necessary ("I understand the driver had to go another way, fine"), so the cost of the diverted route cannot be returned to him.

There is no billing-integrity defect in the ERP lines. Both charged gantries are matched to the trace within the 250 m POL-RD-09(4) radius: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry has a fix at 0.0 m and the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry a fix at 40.25 m (EV-GPS-00103). No gantry was charged that the vehicle did not cross, so the rider gets no full refund of the ERP on a phantom-line theory, and the two lines are genuine pass-through costs of SGD 3.00 and SGD 1.00.

Even on the rider's best case the deviation is modest and not material. Measured on the trace as POL-RD-01 requires, the trip ran 11.18 km (EV-GPS-00103) against a booked optimal of 8.2 km (EV-TRIP-00103) - an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.3%. That clears the 20% / 0.8 km establishment gates but sits well below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality lines, so no MATERIAL deviation is recorded on this trip and the trip_record's rounded 11.2 km convenience copy is not the figure relied on.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to uplift any refund or to refer the driver. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 553 (EV-DPROF-00103), far below the 3-flag and 0.05-ratio thresholds POL-RD-06 sets. No FULL_REFUND uplift is available on this trip and no driver-conduct referral is warranted.

The trace is clean, so the measured excess stands and no escalation is engaged. EV-GPS-00103 carries 175 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval over 100% coverage, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met; there is no impaired stretch, no corroboration requirement, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation. The deviation is measured directly from the trace.

The outcome should preserve the charge. On this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves the fare as charged, which is correct because the excess is exonerated by the closure under POL-RD-03 and the ERP was incurred on a route the rider authorised, barring an ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3). At the very most, and only if the rider's "ok" is not treated as an instruction, the recovery is the off-route ERP pass-through of SGD 4.00 under POL-RD-09(2) - never the SGD 9.00 claimed.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is my decision on trip TRP-00103 (14 July, Bishan to Kallang Wave Mall).

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00103) ran 11.18 km against the booked optimal of 8.2 km (EV-TRIP-00103) — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.3%. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, not the trip record's rounded 11.2 km copy. That clears both establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. It does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality lines, so no MATERIAL deviation is recorded on this trip.

DISTANCE — NO REFUND. The LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00, which covers the trip window, and the trace runs inside the closure geometry. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the entire measured excess is exonerated. There is no excess beyond that cap, so POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance and time charges stand. The $4.15 figure both sides put forward is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against the closure-adjusted optimal; it does not govern here, because POL-RD-02 applies only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation, and POL-RD-03 excuses it in full. Likewise the unadjusted $8.49 comparison is not in play.

ERP — $4.00 REFUNDED. The fare (EV-FARE-00103) carries $4.00 of ERP: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00, against an optimal-route ERP of $0.00. Both gantries are genuinely crossed — the trace passes 0.0 m and 40.25 m from them, inside the 250 m match radius of POL-RD-09(4) — so this is not a phantom-line billing defect and no billing-integrity referral arises. But neither gantry is on the route the rider booked. Under POL-RD-09(2), where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand while off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. The rider did not cause the closure and did not choose the expressway. I therefore refund the off-route ERP of $4.00.

DRIVER'S RIDER-AUTHORISATION ARGUMENT (POL-RD-04 / POL-RD-09(3)) — REJECTED. The driver's message announced the diversion ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah', 08:12:30) and the rider answered 'ok' (08:12:58), but POL-RD-04 requires a RIDER instruction that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on. The rider's reply names no place or road, and neither message carries a waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04's test therefore cannot be run on this record, the clause is unavailable, and the exchange is not a rider-caused detour. POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund.

DRIVER'S NO_ACTION ARGUMENT — REJECTED. Leaving the fare entirely as charged would keep the $4.00 of off-route ERP that POL-RD-09(2) directs be returned.

NO ESCALATION, NO COMPENSATION, NO REFERRALS. Trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is clean (175 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps, max_gap 0 s, 100% coverage, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not met); the advisory is present and current; and the refund is far below the $150 ceiling. No repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 against 553 completed trips_90d), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral applies. No driver compensation is due: the fare billed no less distance than the trace records. The rider's own profile shows deviation_claims_60d 0, so no extra corroboration is demanded.

RESULT. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.00 to the rider (the off-route ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2)); the contested amount was SGD 9.00. The distance and time charges stand. This refund is within the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
